previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 65-year-old woman was admitted with redness and pain around her right knee incision 12 days after total knee arthroplasty, concerning for infection. She was started on IV vancomycin and evaluated by infectious disease. Imaging showed no deep vein thrombosis or abscess, with persistent joint effusion expected post-surgery. A PICC line was placed on hospital day 3 for two weeks of outpatient antibiotic therapy. She remained afebrile, with improving erythema, pain, and mobility. She was discharged home with home health services for IV antibiotics, wound and PICC line care, and instructions for weekly lab monitoring including vancomycin trough levels. She was advised to continue Lovenox for thromboprophylaxis and resume her baseline medications.

close outpatient follow up. If the sensitivies of the
